boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of San Diego
boards.description: Ten currently documented food destinations in San Diego with late-night availability and a direct official source for each location’s hours.

cards.title: Shake Shack Mission Valley
cards.subtitle: 675 Camino De La Reina, Mission Valley
cards.notes: Use the Mission Valley location when you need a documented 2 AM option; its official page lists dine-in, pickup, and delivery.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Valley counter-service stop with 2 AM hours every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Shake Shack’s Mission Valley location lists daily hours of 10:00 AM–2:00 AM and offers dine-in, pickup, and delivery.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 10:00 AM–2:00 AM Sunday through Saturday; dine-in, pickup, and delivery are listed.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger on Camino Del Este
cards.subtitle: 2005 Camino Del Este, Mission Valley
cards.notes: Plan around the posted closing time and use either the drive-thru or dine-in seating listed on the official location page.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Valley burger stop with service documented to 1 AM or later.
cards.evidence_claim: In-N-Out’s 2005 Camino Del Este location lists drive-thru and dine-in seating, closing at 1 AM Sunday–Thursday and 1:30 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official normal hours: 10:30 AM–1:00 AM Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 AM–1:30 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger at Sports Arena
cards.subtitle: 3102 Sports Arena Boulevard, San Diego
cards.notes: Check the posted close before heading over; this location’s official page documents both a drive-thru and dine-in seating.
cards.short_summary: A Sports Arena-area In-N-Out with late posted closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: In-N-Out’s 3102 Sports Arena Boulevard location lists drive-thru and dine-in seating, with normal hours to 1 AM or 1:30 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official normal hours: 10:30 AM–1:00 AM Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 AM–1:30 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger in Kearny Mesa
cards.subtitle: 4375 Kearny Mesa Road, San Diego
cards.notes: This is a late-closing Kearny Mesa option; the official page confirms both seating and drive-thru availability for the location.
cards.short_summary: A Kearny Mesa In-N-Out with documented service past midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: In-N-Out’s 4375 Kearny Mesa Road location lists drive-thru and dine-in seating, closing at 1 AM Sunday–Thursday and 1:30 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official normal hours: 10:30 AM–1:00 AM Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 AM–1:30 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Denny’s on West Point Loma Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 3920 West Point Loma Boulevard, San Diego
cards.notes: Keep this round-the-clock diner in reserve for a sit-down meal or takeout; the official page identifies it as open 24 hours.
cards.short_summary: A nearby 24-hour diner with breakfast, lunch, dinner, and takeout.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its 3920 West Point Loma Boulevard restaurant as open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Denny’s official San Diego location page identifies 3920 W. Point Loma as open 24 hours.

cards.title: Denny’s on Miramar Road
cards.subtitle: 6908 Miramar Road, San Diego
cards.notes: Choose this Miramar Road diner when the timing is uncertain; the location page confirms round-the-clock restaurant hours and walk-ins.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner with walk-ins and takeout listed by the restaurant.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its 6908 Miramar Road restaurant as open 24 hours every day, with walk-ins and takeout available.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists the restaurant as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday; walk-ins and takeout are listed.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Eastman Street
cards.subtitle: 7049 Eastman Street, Clairemont
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the late window, since the official page separately lists earlier dine-in hours for this Clairemont location.
cards.short_summary: A Clairemont drive-thru with official 2 AM daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s 7049 Eastman Street location lists drive-thru hours of 7:00 AM–2:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours until 2:00 AM daily; dine-in hours are listed separately and end earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Mission Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 4401 Mission Boulevard, Pacific Beach
cards.notes: For a later drive-thru option toward Pacific Beach, consult the daily schedule; dine-in service ends earlier than the drive-thru.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Boulevard drive-thru documented to 3 or 4 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s 4401 Mission Boulevard location lists drive-thru service until 3 AM most nights and 4 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official drive-thru hours: until 3:00 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 4:00 AM Thursday–Saturday; dine-in closes earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Aero Drive
cards.subtitle: 9821 Aero Drive, Kearny Mesa
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru late in the evening, and check the day: the official page posts later Thursday through Saturday closing times.
cards.short_summary: An Aero Drive drive-thru with weekday and weekend late-night coverage.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s 9821 Aero Drive location lists drive-thru hours to 1:45 AM on most nights and 2:45 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official drive-thru hours: until 1:45 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 2:45 AM Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell on El Cajon Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 4545 El Cajon Boulevard, San Diego
cards.notes: Treat this as a drive-thru run after the dining room closes; the official page gives a consistent 2 AM drive-thru schedule.
cards.short_summary: An El Cajon Boulevard drive-thru open until 2 AM daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s 4545 El Cajon Boulevard location lists drive-thru hours of 7:00 AM–2:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru hours until 2:00 AM every day; dine-in hours are listed separately and end earlier.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus settings for collaborative work, quiet reading, informal meetups, and outdoor study, documented by USD’s library and university-center pages.

cards.title: Copley Ground Floor Exchange
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · collaborative study level
cards.notes: Bring a project partner or small group and use the ground-floor setting for active learning and conversation at low to moderate volume.
cards.short_summary: A library level designated for collaborative work and extended conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies Copley’s lower level as the Ground Floor Exchange, intended for collaborative work and extended conversations.
cards.access_notes: Library space; follow current library access rules and the published quiet policy.

cards.title: Copley Lounge
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · lower level
cards.notes: Use this lounge when your group needs to compare notes or continue a conversation without moving into the library’s quiet-study areas.
cards.short_summary: A designated lounge where collaboration and extended conversation are allowed.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s library policy allows extended conversations and collaboration in Copley Lounge.
cards.access_notes: Library space; keep conversation within the library’s stated noise expectations.

cards.title: Copley’s group-room network
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · reservable group spaces
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a shared work session, then check in on arrival; these rooms are intended for students working and studying together.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms designed specifically for group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: USD states that Copley group study rooms are a community resource for students to work and study together, and current USD students may reserve them.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is limited to current USD students; group rooms are not for individual study or socializing.

cards.title: Mother Hill Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · absolute quiet study
cards.notes: Choose this reading room for solo, silent concentration; plan calls and group discussion for another campus setting before you enter.
cards.short_summary: A named Copley reading room reserved for absolute quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s quiet policy reserves the Mother Hill Reading Room for absolute quiet study and prohibits talking there.
cards.access_notes: No talking is permitted; observe current Copley Library access rules.

cards.title: Garden Study Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · second-floor Scholarly Living Room
cards.notes: Settle in here for quiet academic work, and save longer conversations for the library’s collaborative spaces on the ground floor.
cards.short_summary: A named room within Copley’s second-floor quiet-study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: USD includes the Garden Study Room in Copley’s second-floor Scholarly Living Room, which is intended for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Extended conversations and loud talking are not appropriate in this second-floor quiet-study area.

cards.title: Journals Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · second-floor reading space
cards.notes: Use this room for focused reading of academic journals or magazines, keeping the space quiet for others working nearby.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room in Copley’s quiet second-floor study area.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists the Journals Reading Room within Copley’s second-floor Scholarly Living Room, intended for quiet academic learning.
cards.access_notes: Not available for reservation or class and organizational meetings, per USD’s room policy.

cards.title: Camino Stacks study spaces
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · ground-floor study seating
cards.notes: Use the study seating in the Camino Stacks when you need a ground-floor work spot where moderate conversation is permitted.
cards.short_summary: Named study spaces among Copley’s Camino Hall stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists study spaces in the Camino Stacks and includes Camino Stacks among ground-floor areas where online meetings are allowed.
cards.access_notes: Located in Copley Library; follow its current access and noise policies.

cards.title: Mother Teresa Plaza
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · informal study and gathering
cards.notes: Meet a friend, spread out for a study break, or use the grass for an informal group session while respecting scheduled reservations.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor plaza used for studying, dining, rallies, and informal gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes Mother Teresa Plaza as a gathering place where students study, dine, hold rallies, meet friends, or relax on the grass.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: Informal use is subject to reservations through USD’s event-registration system.

cards.title: SLP 3rd Floor Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · shaded outdoor seating
cards.notes: Take a laptop or lunch outside under the market umbrellas, then check the reservation schedule if you plan to use the courtyard later in the day.
cards.short_summary: A shaded Student Life Pavilion courtyard for informal lunches and study.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes the SLP 3rd Floor Courtyard as a place to meet for lunch or study, with stated informal-use and reservation periods.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: USD lists informal use weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m. and weekends 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; reservations may take priority at other times.

cards.title: Frank Warren Lounge and Patio
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · open-use patio
cards.notes: Use the patio for a relaxed catch-up or a short outdoor reset; ask University Center Operations or Frank’s Lounge staff before using fire pits.
cards.short_summary: An open-use patio designed for relaxing and catching up with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies the patio in front of Frank’s Lounge as an open-use area for relaxing and catching up with friends, with staff assistance for fire pits.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: Open-use patio; consult University Center Operations or Frank’s Lounge staff for fire-pit assistance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission art, history, and self-guided outings for University of San Diego students and visitors.

cards.title: Browse prints at Hoehn Family Galleries
cards.subtitle: Founders Hall, University of San Diego
cards.notes: Walk through the print and graphic-arts displays in Founders Hall, then use the exhibition brochures or ask a Gallery Guide about a work on view.
cards.short_summary: A free campus gallery stop centered on prints and graphic arts.
cards.evidence_claim: USD states that University Galleries exhibitions and programs are free to the public unless otherwise noted, and lists the Hoehn Family Galleries in Founders Hall.
cards.access_notes: Open only during posted gallery hours; campus weekday parking may require payment, but no ticket or purchase is required for the gallery.

cards.title: See art at the KIPJ Fine Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice, University of San Diego
cards.notes: Check the current KIPJ display before heading over, and pair the visit with a walk through the institute’s public-facing gallery area.
cards.short_summary: A free USD exhibition space inside the Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists KIPJ Fine Art Galleries at the Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice and says University Galleries exhibitions and programs are free to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Check the gallery page for current display availability; tickets and reservations are not required unless USD notes an exception.

cards.title: Visit the David W. May Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saints Tekakwitha and Serra Hall, University of San Diego
cards.notes: Make this a focused art break: view the exhibition in Serra Hall, use the provided interpretive materials, and continue to the nearby Humanities Center Gallery.
cards.short_summary: A free University Galleries stop in Saints Tekakwitha and Serra Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists the David W. May Gallery in Saints Tekakwitha and Serra Hall and says University Galleries exhibitions and programs are free to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted public hours; no gallery ticket or reservation is required unless otherwise noted.

cards.title: Take in the Humanities Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saints Tekakwitha and Serra Hall, University of San Diego
cards.notes: Stop by the Humanities Center Gallery for the current installation, then use the exhibition information to choose one piece for a closer group discussion.
cards.short_summary: A free campus gallery for rotating art and humanities-focused displays.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists the Humanities Center Gallery in Saints Tekakwitha and Serra Hall and says University Galleries exhibitions and programs are free to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted public hours; galleries close for university holidays and may not open outside public hours.

cards.title: Look closely at ICA San Diego Central
cards.subtitle: 1439 El Prado, Balboa Park
cards.notes: Use the gallery’s visual-thinking prompts to compare reactions with friends, then take a short walk through Balboa Park’s public outdoor spaces.
cards.short_summary: Contemporary art in Balboa Park with complimentary admission.
cards.evidence_claim: ICA San Diego states that admission is always complimentary at both locations and identifies its Central location at 1439 El Prado in Balboa Park.
cards.access_notes: Check the ICA site for current open status before going; admission is always free and donations are optional.

cards.title: Spend time with the Timken collection
cards.subtitle: 1500 El Prado, Balboa Park
cards.notes: Pick a small number of paintings or icons to discuss rather than rushing the collection, then step outside to continue exploring Balboa Park.
cards.short_summary: An always-free Balboa Park museum of European, American, and Russian icon art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Timken Museum states that it is always free and provides free guided tours; it is located at 1500 El Prado in Balboa Park.
cards.access_notes: The museum posts its current hours online; admission is free, while transportation or parking can carry separate costs.

cards.title: Follow the Stuart Collection on foot
cards.subtitle: UC San Diego campus, La Jolla
cards.notes: Choose several outdoor works from the map, walk between them at your own pace, and use the digital guide to compare what each artist made for its site.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided contemporary-art walk across UC San Diego.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stuart Collection invites visitors to take a free, self-guided tour of more than 20 sculptures across the UC San Diego campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor sculptures are distributed across campus; follow the collection map and respect any posted building-access restrictions.

cards.title: Explore textile art at Visions
cards.subtitle: 2825 Dewey Road, Liberty Station
cards.notes: Start with the current exhibition, identify a material or technique you want to learn more about, and browse the artist-talk listings before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A free Liberty Station museum devoted to contemporary textile art.
cards.evidence_claim: Visions Museum of Textile Art states that admission is free and lists its location at 2825 Dewey Road in San Diego.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours before travel; museum admission is free, with any optional purchases separate.

cards.entity_name: May S. Marcy Sculpture Court and Garden
cards.title: Meet at the May S. Marcy Sculpture Court
cards.subtitle: San Diego Museum of Art, 1450 El Prado, Balboa Park
cards.notes: Use the free outdoor sculpture court and garden as a low-key meetup, then choose a sculpture to sketch, photograph, or discuss together.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor sculpture-and-garden space at the San Diego Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: The San Diego Museum of Art states that entry to the May S. Marcy Sculpture Court and Garden is free.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission - San Diego Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The sculpture court’s hours vary when private events occur; outdoor entry is free, while museum gallery admission has separate rules.

cards.title: Learn from the Barona Cultural Center & Museum
cards.subtitle: 1095 Barona Road, Lakeside
cards.notes: Plan a daytime visit to view Kumeyaay cultural materials, then use the museum’s Native Plant Garden guide to extend the conversation outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A free museum presenting local Kumeyaay culture and history.
cards.evidence_claim: Barona Cultural Center & Museum states that admission is free and lists public hours Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Check current public hours and call ahead for group tours or research appointments; admission does not require a purchase.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct University of San Diego study environments, ranging from silent reading rooms to reservable collaboration spaces.

cards.title: Mother Rosalie Hill Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library upper level · silent study
cards.notes: Bring work that needs complete concentration; this is Copley’s absolute-quiet room, where talking is not permitted.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent-study room in Copley Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley’s quiet policy reserves the Mother Hill Reading Room for absolute quiet study and prohibits talking there.
cards.access_notes: Located on Copley Library’s upper level; follow the library’s absolute-quiet policy.

cards.title: Journals Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library upper level · quiet study
cards.notes: Settle in with reading or writing work and keep conversation brief; this upper-level room is part of the quiet-study area.
cards.short_summary: A named upper-level reading room within Copley’s quiet-study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley lists the Journals Reading Room on its upper level, and its quiet policy identifies it as part of the Scholarly Living Room for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable; Copley says this room is not intended for classes or organizational meetings.

cards.entity_name: Faculty and Graduate Student Reading Room
cards.title: Faculty and Graduate Student Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library upper level
cards.notes: Use this reading room for quiet academic work if you meet its intended audience; do not plan a class or organization meeting here.
cards.short_summary: An upper-level Copley reading room intended for faculty and graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley lists a Faculty and Graduate Student Reading Room on the upper level; its policy says the Faculty Reading Room is not reservable or intended for class or organizational meetings.
cards.access_notes: Upper-level Copley space; it is not available for reservation.

cards.title: Garden Study Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library upper level · quiet study
cards.notes: Choose this named room when you want a quiet setting for individual reading or laptop work, keeping extended conversation elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A named study room in Copley’s quiet upper-level area.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley’s renovation information names the Garden Study Room, and its quiet policy includes it in the second-floor Scholarly Living Room intended for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Part of Copley’s second-floor quiet-study area; extended conversations are not appropriate.

cards.title: Copley Lounge
cards.subtitle: Copley Library lower level · collaborative work
cards.notes: Bring a partner or project that benefits from discussion; Copley allows extended conversation and collaboration in this lounge.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level library lounge for collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley lists Copley Lounge on the lower level, and its quiet policy permits extended conversations and collaboration there.
cards.access_notes: Use moderate-volume conversation; loud talking is not appropriate anywhere in Copley Library.

cards.title: Camino Stacks Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Copley Library lower level
cards.notes: Head to the Camino Stacks when you need open seating for work that can tolerate the library’s lower-level conversation policy.
cards.short_summary: Named study seating in Copley Library’s Camino Stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley lists study spaces in the Camino Stacks on the lower level and permits online meetings in Camino Stacks seating under its quiet policy.
cards.access_notes: Lower-level library area; moderate talking is allowed, while loud talking is not.

cards.title: Individual Study Rooms 223–226
cards.subtitle: Copley Library upper level · reservation required
cards.notes: Reserve one of rooms 223–226 for solo work; book in hourly increments and check in promptly to keep the reservation.
cards.short_summary: Four reservable Copley rooms designated for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley’s policy identifies rooms 223–226 as individual study rooms available to current USD students, with reservation limits.
cards.access_notes: Current USD students may reserve; bookings are hourly, up to two hours each, and require check-in.

cards.title: Copley Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · reservation required
cards.notes: Reserve with at least one collaborator for an academic project; use the room’s whiteboard and AirMedia connection for shared work.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms equipped for group study and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley has 25 reservable group study rooms for undergraduate and graduate students; its rooms have whiteboards and AirMedia players.
cards.source_title: Group Study Room Information — Copley Library
cards.access_notes: For current USD students and group reservations only; minimum occupancy is two and reservations require check-in.

cards.title: Seminar Room 122
cards.subtitle: Copley Library lower level · group reservation
cards.notes: Book this larger seminar room for a substantial group session; plan for six or more people and bring collaborative coursework.
cards.short_summary: A reservable lower-level seminar room for larger academic groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Copley’s policy identifies Seminar Room 122 as reservable for current USD students, faculty and staff, with a six-person minimum and 14-person maximum.
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; room 122 is limited to groups of 6–14 and two-hour bookings.

cards.title: Learning Commons Town Square
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons · informal gathering space
cards.notes: Use the stadium-style seating for independent work between classes, or coordinate a small-group session around the flexible learning setting.
cards.short_summary: A central informal space in USD’s Learning Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes the Learning Commons Town Square as an informal gathering space with stadium seating for up to 200 people; the building includes collaborative study spaces and supports group and individual study.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: An informal Learning Commons space; confirm any event setup or availability before planning a group meeting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public destinations along the USD-area corridors toward Linda Vista, Old Town, and Mission Bay.

cards.title: Linda Vista Road: public study rooms
cards.subtitle: Linda Vista Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a library card or ask staff about the branch’s public computers and meeting/study room before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A city library branch with public computers and a meeting/study room.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists 19 public-use computers and one meeting/study room at Linda Vista Library, which is on Linda Vista Road.
cards.access_notes: Check the City’s current branch hours before visiting.

cards.title: Presidio Drive: two miles of trails
cards.subtitle: Presidio Drive corridor
cards.notes: Follow the signed Old Presidio Historical Trail for a self-guided walk, and stay on established paths.
cards.short_summary: A historic hilltop park with trails and an interpretive walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Presidio Park has more than two miles of trails and a signed, self-guided Old Presidio Historical Trail.
cards.access_notes: Use designated paths and observe posted park rules.

cards.entity_name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
cards.title: San Diego Avenue: restored historic buildings
cards.subtitle: San Diego Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Start at the visitor center, then use the park map to connect its historic buildings, outdoor exhibits, and programs.
cards.short_summary: A state historic park interpreting early San Diego through buildings and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: California State Parks documents museum exhibitions, restored historic buildings, living-history demonstrations, and special events at the park.
cards.source_title: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
cards.access_notes: The park lists visitor-center and select-museum hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Taylor Street: a transit transfer point
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the station’s posted maps and real-time tools to plan a rail or bus transfer rather than relying on memory.
cards.short_summary: An MTS station at 4009 Taylor Street.
cards.evidence_claim: MTS identifies Old Town Transit Center at 4009 Taylor Street and lists its hours as 6 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: MTS lists station hours as 6 a.m.–9 p.m.; confirm service and platform details before departing.

cards.title: West Mission Bay Drive: playground and water access
cards.subtitle: West Mission Bay Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the marked facilities for a daytime shoreline stop; the City notes a playground, picnic tables, and water access.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay park site with recreation facilities and lifeguard coverage.
cards.evidence_claim: The City places Bonita Cove at 1100 West Mission Bay Drive and lists a playground, water access with lifeguard on duty, picnic tables, grills, and fire rings.
cards.access_notes: The City lists availability from 4 a.m.–10 p.m.; the parking lot closes at 10 p.m.

cards.title: West Vacation Road: model-boat watching
cards.subtitle: West Vacation Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk the pond edge and watch scheduled model sail or power-boat races from the adjacent shaded turf area.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay pond used for sail and power model-boat races and regattas.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Model Yacht Pond is used for sail and power model boats in races and regattas and is reached via West Vacation Road.
cards.access_notes: The City lists the area as open 4 a.m.–2 a.m. and states alcohol is not permitted.

cards.entity_name: Rose Marie Starns South Shores Park
cards.title: Sea World Drive: boat-ramp access
cards.subtitle: Sea World Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the small grassy area and picnic tables for a short waterside stop, keeping clear of the boat-ramp traffic.
cards.short_summary: A small Mission Bay park oriented around boating access.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Rose Marie Starns South Shores Park as a small boating-focused park with a boat ramp, grassy area, picnic tables, and restrooms.
cards.access_notes: The City directs visitors from Sea World Drive and lists the park as open 4 a.m.–2 a.m.; alcohol is not permitted.

cards.title: East Mission Bay Drive: accessible playground
cards.subtitle: East Mission Bay Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the playground, rinse-off shower, picnic tables, or jogging and bike path while observing posted shoreline conditions.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay shoreline site with play, picnic, and path amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists a playground, picnic tables, grills, fire rings, rinse-off shower, and jogging or bike path at Tecolote Shores North.
cards.access_notes: The City lists availability from 4 a.m.–2 a.m., notes no lifeguard is on duty, and prohibits alcohol.

cards.title: Fiesta Island Road: a park-island loop
cards.subtitle: Fiesta Island Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow the posted route from East Mission Bay Drive and use the island’s public roads and designated recreation areas.
cards.short_summary: A named Mission Bay park destination reached from East Mission Bay Drive.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s directions route visitors from Sea World Drive to East Mission Bay Drive and then left to Fiesta Island, with parking throughout the island.
cards.access_notes: Check City notices for events, permits, and any area-specific restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Mariners Way: least-tern observation
cards.subtitle: Mariners Way corridor
cards.notes: Observe from outside fenced nesting areas and do not approach or disturb birds, especially during the breeding season.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay wildlife-tour stop associated with California least terns.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s self-guided wildlife tour identifies Mariner's Point as habitat for the federally listed endangered California least tern and advises that disturbance can cause nest abandonment.
cards.source_title: Self Guided Tour of Wildlife Preserves
cards.access_notes: Respect fences and signs protecting nesting habitat; the City notes June or July as the nesting period.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of San Diego traditions spanning welcome-week rituals, faith gatherings, food, family connection, and Torero philanthropy.

cards.title: Alcalá Bazaar
cards.subtitle: Semester-opening involvement fair
cards.notes: Start with a lap of the booths, then save contacts for organizations or campus centers you want to revisit after classes begin.
cards.short_summary: USD’s biannual kickoff for discovering student organizations, university centers, and local resources.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes the Alcalá Bazaar as a tradition that kicks off each fall and spring semester and connects students with involvement opportunities.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of San Diego, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with campus orientation and mixes landmarks, study space, food, art, and a student event.

cards.title: Start by getting oriented
cards.subtitle: New Student Programs • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Use the orientation hub to confirm your assigned sessions, then introduce yourself to one person before heading out to explore campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the university’s new-student onboarding program.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes undergraduate orientation as including sessions, workshops, social events, and exploration of campus opportunities.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Student Orientation — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Follow the orientation program’s instructions for assigned activities.

cards.title: Get your campus bearings at The Immaculata
cards.subtitle: 5998 Alcalá Park • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Walk to the blue-domed church, pause outside to orient yourself, and check the posted church hours before going inside.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus landmark with regularly posted church hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Immaculata is located on USD’s campus at 5998 Alcalá Park, and its site publishes church hours and Mass times.
cards.access_notes: Church hours are listed as 8:30 a.m.–6 p.m. daily; services may affect quiet access.

cards.title: Cross through Colachis Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between Hughes Administration Center and The Immaculata
cards.notes: Use this central plaza as a walking checkpoint, then look for the fountain area before continuing toward the older campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named central plaza beside The Immaculata.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus-space directory lists Colachis Plaza between Hughes Administration Center and The Immaculata.
cards.source_title: Signature Spaces and Plazas — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; observe any event setup or access notices.

cards.title: See the history inside Founders Chapel
cards.subtitle: Behind Founders Hall • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Take the official virtual or in-person tour option, or stop by during open worship times to see the chapel’s art and architecture.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus chapel with tours and recurring services.
cards.evidence_claim: USD states that Founders Chapel is behind Founders Hall, offers tours, and serves as the main chapel for university Masses.
cards.source_title: Founders Chapel Tours — University of San Diego
cards.access_notes: Tours and services have separate schedules; check the official page before visiting.

cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies Copley Library in Camino Hall and describes its main study areas, reading room, and Special Collections and Archives.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current access and service hours before planning a study session.

cards.title: Take a quiet loop through Garden of the Sea
cards.subtitle: Plaza and garden • University of San Diego
cards.notes: Use the campus map to locate this named garden, then make it a short outdoor reset between the library and your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden for a brief outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus map lists Garden of the Sea among its plazas and gardens.
cards.source_title: University of San Diego Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; use the current campus map and follow any posted access guidance.

cards.entity_name: Fine Art Galleries at the Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice

cards.subtitle: Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice • USD
cards.notes: Look for the Fine Art Galleries in the Kroc Institute, and pair the stop with a walk around the building’s east courtyard.

cards.evidence_claim: USD’s campus map lists Fine Art Galleries in the Joan B. Kroc Institute for Peace and Justice.
